newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-NZ TAKE COMMAND VS ENGLAND IN TEST.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-NZ TAKE COMMAND VS ENGLAND IN TEST.

text.p: A maiden test century by Stephen Fleming helped New Zealand take command against England, bringing the total to 338 for six wickets at lunch on the second day of the first test on Saturday.
Lefthander Fleming, playing his 23rd test and his 39th test innings, reached his century in fine style, driving left-arm spinner Phil Tufnell through mid-off to the boundary.
It took him 199 balls and included 16 fours and a six.
Since making 92 against India on his test debut in 1994, Fleming has often promised to deliver his first century, but instead has had to be content with 10 half centuries.
That changed today when he carried on his dominance of the England attack, having begun the day on 58.
With Chris Cairns, Fleming put New Zealand in a strong position at lunch, at 338 for six, having begun the day at 233 for five.
Fleming was on 105 at the interval and captain Lee Germon was on two.
Fleming and Cairns scored just seven runs from the first seven overs of the day, but the runs came freely after that.
Cairns went to his sixth test half century by slamming Tufnell into the crowd at extra cover.
Their 100 partnership came in 173 balls as they moved to shut England out of the test.
Cairns had one life, on 20, when left armer Alan Mullally dropped a return catch, one handed to his left.
He was dismissed 12 minutes before lunch when he drove at a wide ball from allrounder Craig White and gave wicketkeeper Alec Stewart his third catch of the innings.
Cairns' 67 came from 113 balls and included seven fours and two sixes.
With Fleming, he had added 118 in 201 balls for the sixth wicket.
